mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS ≤ 0.1%) indicates an accommodative monetary policy environment that reduces the discount rate for equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS ≤ 0.1% (t-test p > 0.05 for mean return > 0).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeding 5.5% signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which typically leads to reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE > 5.5% (t-test p > 0.05 for mean return < 0).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates weakening consumer demand, which triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when both HOUST < 900 and RSAFS < 440000 (t-test p > 0.05 for mean return < 0).

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS rising at least 0.25% in 3 months), the increased cost of capital reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS rises > 0.25% in prior 3 months (t-test p > 0.05 for mean return < 0).

mechanism_narrative: Strong housing market activity (HOUST > 900) is a leading indicator of economic expansion, which typically supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when HOUST > 900 (t-test p > 0.05 for mean return > 0).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO < 100) indicates contraction in manufacturing and services, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO < 100 (t-test p > 0.05 for mean return < 0).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in GDP growth (GDPC1 < 16000) and retail sales (RSAFS < 440000) signals a weakening economic foundation, which triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when both GDPC1 < 16000 and RSAFS < 440000 (t-test p > 0.05 for mean return < 0).

mechanism_narrative: During a period of strong labor market growth (PAYEMS increasing > 0.5% in 3 months), the rising employment base supports consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when PAYEMS increases > 0.5% in prior 3 months (t-test p > 0.05 for mean return > 0).
